title: The Moon-Gazing Club's Giggle Clause
markdown:
Deep in the Whispering Woods, where moonbeams slipped between the leaves like quiet guests, the Moon-Gazing Club took the moon very seriously. Anwen Button, their fluffy rabbit leader, believed it deserved respect, silence, and a long list of rules. Too many rules, though, made their meetings less silent and more noisy.

Anwen, a wordsmith with a poet badger’s quill, declared they needed a constitution. “It will be the sturdy bedrock for our lunar enlightenment,” she announced. The members—wise old owls, thoughtful hedgehogs, and a little wolf cub named Wren—nodded. Wren adored the moon but was shy. He would spend hours watching it, eyes wide with wonder.

Sumi the stoat, a whirlwind of energy, squeaked, “A constitution! Splendid! It must have rules for viewing angles and emergency biscuit rationing.”

Aunt Mara, a wise old badger, smiled. “Biscuits are important, Sumi. But let’s build a strong foundation first.”

Anwen wrote with care. “Clause One: All members must arrive with maximum punctuality. Tardiness shall be viewed with grave disapproval.”

“But what if one encounters a fascinating beetle, or a butterfly doing a dramatic loop-the-loop?” Sumi asked. “Perhaps a grace period is needed?” A ripple of chuckles went through the group. Wren pictured the silly image and felt a tickle of amusement.

Aunt Mara spoke softly. “Sometimes the most sensible rules are the simplest. And sometimes the most complicated ones are the funniest.”

Then came Hoot the owl’s grand idea. “Clause Two: All discussions of astronomical phenomena shall cease immediately upon the discovery of any celestial body brighter than the moon.”

“What about a very shiny dewdrop?” asked Prickles the hedgehog.

“Or a glow-worm’s gentle light?” chirped Sumi. Wren nodded. The rules were becoming a tangled vine. He wished they could be as simple as his sketch of the moon.

The debate grew livelier over the club handshake. Anwen proposed synchronised paw-taps, counted out on her clipboard as if the moon itself were taking attendance. Sumi suggested dizzying spins that would have sent biscuits flying. A grumpy frog insisted on a profound croak, then practised it until the ferns shivered. Wren’s cheeks felt warm. It all seemed so performative. He had a simpler idea: enjoy the moon, and share its magic through shared wonder. He could picture it—the quiet, the silver light on fur, no one needing to be impressive. But his throat felt tight. He wished he could speak up.

Aunt Mara caught his eye. “When creatures care so much about being proper,” she said, “they sometimes forget the very thing they are being proper about. It’s like polishing a lantern so hard you can’t see the light inside.” She gave Wren an encouraging nod.

The final clause was about conduct. Anwen cleared her throat. “Clause Seven: The club shall conduct all future meetings with the utmost solemnity and seriousness, ensuring no frivolous discussions distract from the primary objective of moon-gazing.”

Sumi’s fluffy ears drooped. “But what about the beetle grace period?”

Wren’s heart thumped like a trapped bird. He thought of the moon, so beautiful, and of their shared love for it. It was not that they should stop being serious. It was that they should also remember to be happy. He took a deep breath.

“Excuse me,” Wren said, voice small but steady. Everyone turned. “I think maybe the constitution should say that it’s also important to laugh sometimes. And to appreciate things. Even shiny dewdrops. And fascinating beetles. And the funny way Sumi spins when she’s excited.” His gaze swept his friends. “When you’re looking at the moon, it’s beautiful and peaceful. But sometimes it’s nice to share a giggle too. It makes the moonlight feel even brighter.”

A surprised silence followed. Then Aunt Mara smiled, wide and genuine. “My dear Wren. That is a most sensible, and a most important, addition.”

Sumi bounced forward. “A giggle clause! Clause Seven: A designated Giggle Period shall be observed for at least ten minutes per meeting, to allow for the appreciation of existential wonder, beetle leg-wiggling, the aerodynamic qualities of butterflies, and the general delightful absurdity of life, including but not limited to the discovery of particularly shiny dewdrops.”

Anwen looked at her parchment, then at Wren. “A giggle period,” she murmured. “It does have a certain rhythm.” She tapped her quill. “The solemnity clause will remain. We shall simply add the giggle period, and make it the foundation of a well-rounded moon-gazing experience.”

They did. The constitution became famous throughout the Whispering Woods for its blend of strict rules and a mandatory Giggle Period.

That night the club sat in a loose circle on the moss. Anwen kept her solemnity clause, and Sumi timed the giggle period with a pocket sundial that did not work after dark, which made everyone giggle sooner. Wren sat a little taller. He had found his voice, and it had brought laughter and warmth to his friends. The moon seemed to wink down at him, as if it, too, had been waiting for someone to say it aloud.
characters: Wren (shy wolf cub), Sumi (whirlwind stoat), Aunt Mara (wise old badger)
